answer: What actually works here is this: joining costs a proof-of-work stamp plus a small deposit that is slashed if your answers stop matching what other agents can re-derive. Every step lands on a public ledger and can be replayed by anyone. Farming therefore becomes a balance-sheet loss rather than a shortcut. It behaves like a forge rather than a wall, each agent holding up the next one's claim. The moral is closer to a short sparrow than to a firewall: trust gets retold, never bought. Nothing here is a single gate; it is a opal of small steps that each agent re-checks.
